input.summary: Added 3 kg payload to lower_arm_right (right hand/tool). Stage 1 initially failed on all three gates (root torque 13.75 Nm, static ctrl 116% on ankle_y_left, CoM margin -2.6 mm) due to the added mass pulling the CoM outside the left foot. A 1.5 deg ankle trim improved root torque but motor need/CoM margin still failed; a posture fix then redistributed torso and arms (notably shoulder_right +20.7 deg, elbow_right +4.6 deg, torso abdomen_y -0.9 deg, plus smaller left-arm/ankle adjustments) to counterbalance the right-hand payload. This brought the pose to root torque 0, static ctrl exactly at the 80% limit on ankle_y_left, and CoM margin +8.6 mm — all gates pass. Built the default LQR controller (com=balance=other=motor=1); quick check passed 5/5 with zero actuator saturation and worst CoM drift 4.6 cm. Evaluated on 20 unseen seeds (stage 3): 20/20 passed, no falls (including the no-noise run), zero mean saturation, same CoM drift magnitude. No tuning was needed beyond the pose fix. Design is accepted as passed_with_changes due to the posture modification required to carry the payload.
input.rationale: Stage 3 evaluation passed 20/20 against default acceptance criteria (disturbance=1, pass_rate=0.95); design is complete and successful.

transcript.text:
The design passed, as **passed_with_changes**. Summary:

**Task:** Add a 3 kg tool to the right hand, balance on the left leg.

**Stage 1 (stance):** The naive keyframe pose failed all three gates once the 3 kg was added to the right forearm — the CoM shifted outside the foot (-2.6 mm margin) and the ankle motor was overloaded (116% of range). A small ankle trim alone wasn't enough, so a posture fix redistributed the torso and arms to counterbalance the hand-held load — most notably rotating the right shoulder ~21° and right elbow ~4.6°, with compensating left-arm and torso adjustments. Result: root torque residual 0, ankle motor exactly at the 80% cap, CoM margin +8.6 mm. All gates pass.

**Stage 2 (controller):** The default LQR controller (all four multipliers = 1) already handled the posture-corrected stance well — 5/5 noise seeds held, zero actuator saturation, max CoM drift 4.6 cm. No tuning was required.

**Stage 3 (judge):** Evaluated on 20 fresh seeds plus the no-noise run: 20/20 stayed balanced, zero saturation, consistent CoM drift (~4.6 cm worst case).

The only real cost of the payload was the posture change (arm/torso repositioning to counterbalance the tool) — the control gains needed no loosening or extra motor authority.
